jobs.specialization: Education -The Child & The Curriculum in Early Childhood Education
jobs.description: Assistant Professor/Instructor of Education -The Child & The Curriculum in Early Childhood Education Print Assistant Professor/Instructor of Education -The Child & The Curriculum in Early Childhood Education Location Georgetown, Texas 78626 Job Type Faculty - Part Time, Exempt, Contract based Job Number 202600052 Division Academic Affairs Department Education Dept Opening Date 05/08/2026 Description Benefits ABOUT US Located in Georgetown, Texas, Southwestern University is an independent, four-year undergraduate institution offers a top-ranked integrated arts and sciences curriculum that incorporates the humanities, fine arts, social sciences, and natural sciences. At Southwestern University, we are committed to fostering an environment where every individual feels respected, valued, and empowered. We believe that a thriving community is built on the strength of varying perspectives and experiences, and we strive to create an atmosphere of mutual respect and understanding. Our actions are guided by a commitment to fairness, openness, and the belief that our differences are what make us stronger as a whole. POSITION OVERVIEW The Department of Education at Southwestern University invites applications for a part-time Instructor/Adjunct Professor to teach The Child and the Curriculum in Early Childhood Education in Spring 2027. This course introduces early childhood pedagogy, curriculum, and settings. Students examine typical and atypical development, play development, and culturally responsive, play-based strategies. Posting Details Position Information Posting Number F00801P Position Title Assistant/Associate Professor Department Biology Location Arlington Job Family Faculty Position Status Full-time Rank Tenure-track Work Hours Standard Open to External and Internal FLSA Exempt Duration Funding expected to continue Pay Basis Monthly Benefits Eligible Yes Job Summary The Department of Biology in the College of Science, at the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) (http://www.uta.edu/biology/), invites applications for a Tenure-Track faculty position in Genomics at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. We seek to expand our strength in Genomics by recruiting a faculty member who will establish a nationally recognized, collaborative research program and contribute to our growing research community. Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to, spatially-resolved functional genomics, cell signaling, genetics and epigenetics studies and other integrative approaches to understanding biological function. We seek applicants whose research uses genomic and related approaches at any level of biological organization across model and non-model organisms. Applications of integrative, mechanistic, and systems-level approaches to investigate the physiological, genetic, and epigenetic mechanisms that govern biological function, health, and disease would align well with the Department’s long-term mission. jobs.description: Assistant/Associate Professor in Integrative Shellfish BiologyApply now DescriptionThe Department of Marine Science and Marine Science Institute at The University of Texas at Austin (UTMSI) is seeking an assistant or associate professor in the field of Integrative Shellfish Biology. Fields of study can include, but are not limited to, physiology, functional biology, ecology and evolution, reproduction and development, disease, and host–pathogen interactions, as well as fisheries science and mariculture. We seek to fill this position in coordination with the development of a new state-of-the-art oyster mariculture research facility that will be located at the University of Texas Marine Science Institute’s Fisheries and Mariculture Laboratory in Port Aransas, Texas. In doing so, UTMSI is building the capacity to advance commercial oyster mariculture activities in the state of Texas, which includes facilities for broodstock husbandry, spawning, larval rearing, and spat production. As such, we are most interested in candidates that can make use of these facilities and contribute to the broader mission of the facility, but we strongly encourage applicants with both fundamental and applied research portfolios to apply. The Department of Marine Science is housed in the College of Natural Sciences and is home to an expanding group of 15 faculty who are engaging in research across a broad range of marine science disciplines. The successful applicant is expected to establish an internationally recognized, extramurally funded research program and mentor research personnel, teach at the graduate and undergraduate levels, and contribute to departmental service. The position is located at the University of Texas Marine Science Institute in Port Aransas, Texas, which is located 3.5 hours from Austin but holds strong collaborative ties to the research community on the university’s main campus, including the Department of Integrative Biology and the Jackson School of Geosciences. The Institute is home to the Department’s graduate degree program and has state-of-the-art laboratories and seawater-supplied facilities for experimental research. The Institute is also in close proximity to a variety of marine habitats that include near-pristine to anthropogenically altered estuarine ecosystems (oyster reefs, seagrasses, mangroves, saltmarshes, microbial mats, open water), with salinities ranging from oligohaline to hypersaline, as well as near- and offshore habitats of the Gulf of Mexico. The Institute hosts the Mission-Aransas National Estuarine Research Reserve, Beaufort Lagoon Ecosystems Long Term Ecological Research program, Fisheries and Mariculture Laboratory complex, and the Center for Coastal Ocean Science. The Institute also houses full-service core analytical facilities, a fleet of research vessels, and will take ownership of a new 78-ft All American Marine research vessel in spring 2027. This vessel will be fully equipped and specifically designed to support diverse research activities, including biological, geological, biogeochemical, and physical oceanography.QualificationsRequired Qualifications Applicants must hold a PhD in marine science, biology, fisheries science, or a closely related field at the time of appointment. Postdoctoral or equivalent research experience is expected. Candidates must demonstrate the potential to establish (Assistant Professor) or an established record of (Associate Professor) an independent, externally funded research program in shellfish biology or a related discipline, along with a commitment to graduate and undergraduate teaching and mentorship. Appointment Rank The rank of appointment (Assistant or Associate Professor) will be commensurate with the candidate's experience and record. The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership for the Dunn Center, engage in influential scholarly work, contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in church music, and cultivate meaningful connections among the academy, the church, and the broader field of Christian music and worship. About Church Music and the Dunn Center for Christian Music Studies Church Music at Baylor brings together rigorous musical study, theological reflection, research, and practical formation for service to the church. Students pursue undergraduate and graduate pathways in Church Music, including master’s and doctoral study and a joint M.Div./M.M. with George W. Truett Theological Seminary. The Dunn Center for Christian Music Studies extends this work through research initiatives, conferences and public programs, visiting artists and scholars, church and professional partnerships, and global Music & Missions opportunities. Faculty and staff work collaboratively to prepare musicians and scholars for thoughtful, creative, and faithful leadership in a wide range of Christian denominations and communities. About the Baylor School of Music : At the Baylor School of Music, faith and artistry meet purpose. Our faculty guide exceptional students through a rigorous, musically rich education, where every performance, composition, and collaboration reflects excellence and depth. From captivating performers to musical scholars to contemporary innovators, Baylor shapes versatile artists and educators who thrive creatively and professionally.  What  sets the Baylor School of Music apart? A vibrant community of 300 students from  across the country  and around the globe. Award-winning ensembles that have performed at every major national conference

jobs.description: Job Title Assistant/Associate Professor of English, Writing Studies Agency Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi Department College Of Liberal Arts Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Corpus Christi, Texas Job Type Faculty Job Description The Department of English at Texas A&M University–Corpus Christi invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track faculty position in Rhetoric and Composition, beginning Fall 2027. The appointment may be made at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications, level of expertise, and professional experience. The department is seeking an experienced writing program administrator to support the First-Year Writing Program. Applicants should demonstrate a record of excellent teaching and have an active, current scholarly agenda in writing program administration. Teaching expectations will include a 3/3 course load (not including course release time for program administration) comprising first-year writing courses and upper-division undergraduate courses in writing studies. Candidates will also have the opportunity to offer graduate courses and mentor students in the department’s English MA program. Administrative duties, when part of the faculty’s appointment, will include development and assessment of writing curricula and outcomes and initiating faculty development opportunities to support writing pedagogy in the program. The Department of English offers undergraduate English majors a choice in either a Writing or Literary Studies emphasis, curricula for secondary English certification, certificates in Writing for Non-Profits, social media, and TESOL, and minors in Technical and Professional Writing, Creative Writing, and Literary Studies. The graduate program provides an interdisciplinary educational experience in a generalist MA in English by requiring advanced study in Writing Studies, Literary Studies, and Applied Linguistics. At TAMU-CC, our first-year writing program is informed by research on how people write, how they learn, and what they need to be flexible, adept writers ready to take on new challenges. Our program works to teach writing in ways that connect students to their majors and coordinate with the demands of other first-year classes. As a program, we want to help students understand that writing, language, and rhetoric are all multifaceted and evolving; we want students to be able to use writing and language in ways that will help them achieve their goals. Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a vibrant, Hispanic and Minority Serving R2 Doctoral Research Institution that proudly provides a solid academic reputation, renowned faculty, and highly rated degree programs since 1947. The University has a heritage of teaching excellence with innovation in research and community engagement as part of the distinguished Texas A&M System. The only university in the nation is located on its own island, at the heart of the Texas Gulf Coast. With palm tree lined pathways throughout the campus, nearby natural wetlands, a scenic hike-and-bike trail and pristine views of the beach and bays, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a first-choice institution. As part of a vibrant academic community dedicated to excellence in teaching, research, and service, this role offers the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to a university that values innovation, collaboration, and inclusive growth. Join us in advancing knowledge and transforming lives—on campus and beyond. Tarleton State University continues to grow its impact across Texas, with four distinct campuses located in Stephenville, Fort Worth, RELLIS-Bryan and Waco , along with a robust online community that extends our reach even further. At the heart of it all is Stephenville , where Tarleton State offers a dynamic environment for faculty and staff. From a lively live music scene and numerous local festivals to rich traditions rooted in the surrounding community, Stephenville provides a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere. No matter where you're located—on campus or online—you are part of a mission that transforms lives and makes a difference across the state of Texas and beyond. ________________________________________________________________________ Important Immigration Information: A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate. ________________________________________________________________________ At Tarleton State University Division of Health Sciences, we are committed to educating individuals who will become competent leaders dedicated to advancing wellness in the communities they serve. As we embark on the development of the Doctor of Physical Therapy program, we invite applications for core faculty at the Assistant/Associate/Full Professor Clinical-Track of Physical Therapy. Applicants who are board-certified clinical specialists in orthopedics, neurologic, or cardiovascular pulmonary physical therapy will be prioritized. Reporting to the Director of the Physical Therapy Program, faculty members will teach courses and content within their areas of expertise, and build and maintain authentic, collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholder. The successful candidate will actively engage in mentoring and guiding doctoral students through their academic and research endeavors, fostering a supportive and enriching environment within our DPT program. jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston is seeking a board-certified/board-eligible diagnostic abdominal radiologist for a faculty position in the Department of Diagnostic and Interventional Imaging to join a busy clinical and academic abdominal radiology service. McGovern Medical School primarily provides imaging services at Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center and Harris Health LBJ Hospital. We also provide coverage at several outpatient imaging centers. The section is highly integrated with the UT departments of Oncology, Gastroenterology, Urology, Gynecology, and Trauma. Position Key Accountabilities: Providing, reading, and interpreting diagnostic services, including radiography, fluoroscopy, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, sonography, and positron emission tomography, as well as limited procedures. Providing excellent patient care, fostering a culture of learning and growth, and driving innovation within the section.Creating and implementing new or revised protocols that address identified areas for improvement and leverage new technologies; integrating fluoroscopy equipment and techniques that enhance safety and improve image quality. Assessing current fluoroscopy protocols for abdominal imaging procedures, considering factors like patient safety, image quality, and efficiency.Teaching residents, fellows, and medical students in radiology. Participating in consultation at the reading room and tumor board. The academic research opportunities at UTHealth Houston are abundant. The basic science section of the department is well-equipped (with research dedicated 3.0 and 7.0 T MR units) and well-staffed with physicists. Academic activities are strongly encouraged and supported. UTHealth Houston offers excellent benefits. Qualifications: ACGME-accredited Diagnostic Radiology Residency Program (or equivalent).Fellowship training in Abdominal Imaging (or equivalent).ABR certified or ABR eligible. Texas Medical License or be eligible to obtain a faculty temporary License. Qualified applicants must demonstrate a commitment to excellence, discovery, and service, have the potential to be outstanding in their field of expertise, and share an interest in fulfilling the common goals of McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston.

jobs.description: Back to Listings Assistant/Associate/Full Professor: Open Rank Pharmaceutical Sciences Location Kingsville and College Station Open Date 10/23/2023 Position ID 124317 Description The Texas A&M Rangel School of Pharmacy invites nominations and applications for two faculty openings in the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, one in Kingsville and the other in College Station, in the areas of biomedical/pharmaceutical sciences, or related areas. These are full-time 11-month, tenure-track/tenure review upon hire positions, with a earliest possible start date of Spring 2024. The position type (Tenure Track or Tenure Review Upon Hire), faculty rank (Assistant/Associate or Full Professor) as well as salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Responsibilities would include: 1. making contributions to research in the department related to one or multiple broader areas of biomedical, pharmaceutical, or related areas, as well as developing and maintaining a sustainable and extramurally-funded research program, 2. teaching/assisting in the delivery of the School’s PharmD and/or PhD in pharmaceutical sciences programs, 3. mentoring and advising of students and postdocs, and 4. providing service within and outside the school, and contributing to establishing a positive, supportive and collaborative environment. Current research in the department with potential for collaboration include: drug delivery and formulations, cardiovascular, diabetes, oncology, infectious disease, as well as pharmacoepidemiology, and pharmacoeconomics. There are ample opportunities to engage in collaborative research, conduct applied and contract research, and contribute to enhancing the research portfolio as well as the teaching and service mission of the School and Texas A&M University. The successful candidates will be provided with a competitive start-up package. Qualifications Candidates should have earned a Ph.D. degree in Biomedical and/or Pharmaceutical Sciences or a related field and have excellent oral and written communication and interpersonal skills. Candidates with a track record of effective scholarship, funding, previous teaching experience and research interests that complement the strengths of the school will be given preference. The track record and history of accomplishments in teaching, research and service should be commensurate with the position type and the rank applied for. This position provides opportunities for individuals with a strong commitment to an academic career with emphasis on research, instruction, and service. Application Instructions Individuals interested in this position should submit a cover letter, curriculum vita, personal statement (describing research philosophy and interests), and names and contact information for three references through the Interfolio system at the link located here: http://apply.interfolio.com/134257. If you have any questions about this position, please direct them to Dr. Fadi Khasawneh, Department Head of Pharmaceutical Sciences, at fkhasawneh@tamu.edu (361-221-0755) with copy to Ms. Dalia Cavazos, Administrative Associate V, at dgcavazos@tamu.edu (361-221-0731) Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer. The University is aware that attracting and retaining exceptional faculty often depends on meeting the needs of two careers and therefore has a Dual Career Program.

jobs.description: Associate or Full Professor of Curriculum and Instruction with a Specialization in Learning TechnologiesApply now DescriptionThe Department of Curriculum and Instruction in the College of Education at The University of Texas at Austin seeks a faculty member at the associate professor or full professor level whose scholarship advances Learning Technologies. Although the primary appointment falls within the Learning Technologies program area in the Department of Curriculum and Instruction, the successful candidate will have the ability to lead college-wide initiatives related to Learning Technologies. A secondary appointment in the Department of Kinesiology and Health Education, Special Education, Educational Psychology, or Educational Leadership and Policy will also be considered. The successful candidate will have a strong record of research focusing on the applications, implications, and innovations of Learning Technologies in EC–12, higher education, professional learning, or informal contexts. Such scholarship may include, but is not limited to, studies of generative AI in teaching and learning; learning analytics and educational data science; human-AI interaction; the design of AI- and technology-enriched learning environments; technology-supported curriculum design and assessment; technology-rich teacher education and professional learning; and accessible, culturally responsive, and community-engaged learning technologies. We welcome scholarship that advances educational innovations while critically examining the pedagogical, ethical, social, cultural, and policy implications of AI and emerging technologies. The successful candidate will have a record of securing external grants to support a research program with meaningful impact. The successful candidate will teach and mentor undergraduate students and graduate students. In Learning Technologies, a graduate program, they may teach courses in areas such as instructional design, learning theory, research methods, design-based research, online and blended learning, educational data and AI, technology-supported curriculum and instruction, and teacher education. The successful candidate will also show interest in participating in existing, or creating new, interdisciplinary collaborations that explore innovative and responsible uses of AI and Learning Technologies. The Department of Pediatrics at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) John Sealy School of Medicine is seeking an outstanding physician-scientist in Pediatric Nephrology to join our growing academic program. This is an exceptional opportunity for a pediatric nephrologist with a strong commitment to research, clinical excellence, education, and academic leadership to develop and lead an independent research program while providing high-quality care to children with kidney disease.
The Opportunity
The successful candidate will join a collaborative Pediatric Nephrology program providing comprehensive care for children with renal disorders across UTMB's clinical network, including Galveston and League City. The division provides care for children with a broad spectrum of kidney conditions, including hypertension, chronic kidney disease, congenital and acquired renal disorders, and disorders of bladder and urinary function.
The physician-scientist will have the opportunity to:
• Develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program in pediatric nephrology or a related area.
• Pursue innovative basic, translational, clinical, or population health research relevant to kidney health in children.
• Collaborate with investigators across Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, and UTMB's research centers and institutes.

Research Environment
UTMB offers a highly collaborative academic environment with extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary investigation. The institution has more than 10 research centers and three institutes, as well as the Galveston National Laboratory, providing opportunities for collaboration across basic, translational, and clinical research programs. UTMB is currently ranked among the nation's leading academic institutions in NIH research funding.
We are particularly interested in candidates whose research complements or expands existing expertise in areas such as:
• Pediatric kidney disease and chronic kidney disease
• Hypertension and cardiovascular-kidney health
• Kidney development and congenital kidney disorders
• Glomerular and tubular diseases
• Acute kidney injury
• Kidney disease biomarkers and precision medicine
• Translational nephrology
• Clinical and outcomes research
• Health disparities and population health
• Innovative approaches to prevention and treatment of pediatric kidney disease
Candidates with established NIH funding or a strong record of obtaining extramural support are especially encouraged to apply. Early-career investigators with strong research potential and a compelling vision for developing an independent program are also encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will:
• Provide compassionate, evidence-based care to children with kidney disease.
• Participate in inpatient and outpatient Pediatric Nephrology services.
• Teach and mentor learners at multiple levels.
• Develop collaborative research initiatives and pursue extramural funding.
• Publish scholarly work in high-impact peer-reviewed journals.
• Participate in departmental and institutional committees and academic activities.
• Contribute to the strategic growth of Pediatric Nephrology at UTMB.

jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston, a leading academic health center, invites applications for a full-time non-tenure clinical track Associate Professor or Professor position in the Department of Pediatrics, Division of Nephrology and Hypertension. The division provides care for infants, children, and adolescents with all forms of kidney disease and high blood pressure, and inpatient services and consultations for children at Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital, Harris Health Lyndon B. Johnson Hospital, and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. Inpatient services include all dialysis modalities and CRRT to support a highly complex patient population, including NICU, PICU, and CVICU. Ambulatory services at the main campus of the Texas Medical Center include a dedicated pediatric hypertension clinic, general nephrology clinics, a tuberous sclerosis clinic, and a fetal consultation clinic. In addition, the division has a dedicated onco-nephrology clinic at MD Anderson Cancer Center, general nephrology and hypertension clinics throughout the Houston metro area, with plans for additional satellite outreach clinics, and renal transplant clinics at the Memorial Hermann Hospital. Our chronic dialysis unit has been relocated to a new state-of-the-art, 11-station, dedicated pediatric dialysis unit at Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital, supported by a dedicated team of nurses, child-life team, social worker, and renal dietitian. The new dialysis unit supports the growth of the ESRD population and of the active pediatric renal transplant program at Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital. The division has a pediatric nephrology fellowship program with a long tradition of graduating future leaders in the field. The division is an active participant in CKiD, RAFT, NAPRTCS, PNRC, and IROC, with plans to join SCOPE. Excellent teaching opportunities are available for medical students, residents, and fellows. The selected candidate will contribute to the department’s mission to educate health science professionals, discover and translate advances in the biomedical and social sciences, and model the best practices in clinical care and public health through research, teaching, clinical service, administrative activities, and other services. The new faculty will join a dynamic team of 6 Nephrologists, a Physician Assistant, and a Nurse Practitioner with various clinical and academic interests. The Division of Pediatric Nephrology & Hypertension is supported by dedicated pediatric nephrology and dialysis nurses, a full-time research coordinator, transplant coordinators, a social worker, a dietitian, and administrative staff. Position Key Accountabilities: The selected candidate will provide direct patient care in the clinic and hospital settings, share call and in-service coverage, and participate in outreach clinics in satellite locations. · Inpatient/consultation and outpatient services at Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital, MD Anderson Cancer Center, with the possibility to expand services to additional future sites.· Responsibilities in the Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital Dialysis Unit and the education and training of medical students, residents, and fellows. · Interest in academic achievement and is encouraged to conduct research and quality improvement projects in their area of interest, with opportunities to develop new programs.Qualifications: M.D. or D.O. degree and be board-certified in Pediatrics Board-eligible/certified in Pediatric Nephrology. Qualified applicants must demonstrate a commitment to excellence, discovery, and service, have the potential to be outstanding in their field of expertise, and share an interest in fulfilling the common goals of McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston.

jobs.description: 46324BR Asst/Assoc/Professor, Department of Surgery, General Surgery Surgery Dept Ode Genl Odessa Introduction Nationally recognized as a Great College to Work For, TTUHSC provides much more than just a job! Enjoy excellent benefits, including paid leave, retirement plans, wellness programs, health insurance and so much more. Ready to start building a rewarding career in a positive environment where you can develop and thrive? Join us as we change the future of health care. About TTUHSC Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center is enriching the lives of others by educating students, providing excellent patient care, and advancing knowledge through innovative research. TTUHSC graduates more health care professionals than any other health care institution in the state, conferring 24.2% of all degrees and certificates awarded from health-related institutions in Texas. By providing comprehensive clinical services to more than 10 million individuals across 121 counties, TTUHSC is dedicated to advancing the health of people throughout Texas and beyond. This is where world-class education meets compassionate patient care – and we believe that our people are the reason for our institution’s lasting success and bright future.Being part of the TTUHSC team means being part of an innovative and supportive community that empowers each individual to do their best work. Through our values-based culture, TTUHSC is committed to cultivating an exceptional workplace community with a positive culture that puts people first. Visa Information TTUHSC, at its sole discretion, may initiate new H-1B I-129 visa petitions in accordance with the directive issued by Governor Abbott. Approval from the Texas Workforce Commission is required. On a limited, case-by-case basis, the institution may also sponsor eligible individuals for change-of-status or change-of-employer petitions for qualifying positions. TTUHSC will not pay the $100,000 fee, if applicable. Position Description Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (TTUHSC) Permian Basin Department of Surgery. Our program is rooted in a rigorous, evidence-based educational environment that emphasizes clinical excellence, surgical proficiency, and continuous professional development. As part of our surgery residency program, we are committed to cultivating surgeons who are very technically skilled, as well as focusing on professionalism, exemplifying integrity, inclusivity, and the highest standards of patient-centered care with compassion and kindness.Located in the heart of the Permian Basin—the nation’s largest petroleum-producing region and one of its fastest-growing populations—our department plays a vital role in expanding and strengthening the surgical workforce to meet the urgent healthcare needs of this underserved area. Our mission is to train surgeons who are equipped to serve diverse communities with empathy, cultural competence, and clinical excellence in the Permian Basin or any other community.The General Surgeon will have block time scheduled with our community hospital(s), participating in call coverage rotation and maintaining clinical time for pre and post surgical consultation. Opportunities for GME leadership with the Residency and Clerkship Programs. Da Vinci Robot opportunities at community hospitals. Major/Essential Functions Diagnose and manage a broad array of medical conditions through preoperative, operative and postoperative care.Provide inpatient and outpatient care of surgical patients.Procedures to include both emergent and non-emergent conditions.Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team and refer patients as appropriate.Educate patients on treatment plans, medications and pre and post operation care.Complete medical records accurately and completely in a timely manner.Participate in the training of medical students and residents. Required Qualifications MD/DO or equivalent,Completion of, or in the process of completing an ACGME accredited General Surgery Residency,A

jobs.title: Automation & Advanced Manufacturing Instructor
jobs.description: Automation & Advanced Manufacturing Instructor Primary Purpose: Provide high-quality instruction and workforce training in automation and advanced manufacturing, with primary responsibility for training in battery construction and assembly and the automated manufacturing of parts. The instructor will develop and deliver classroom, laboratory, and hands-on learning experiences that prepare students and incumbent workers for modern manufacturing environments supporting regional industry partners. Qualifications: Education Associate degree in Advanced Manufacturing, Automation, Mechatronics, Industrial Technology, Engineering Technology, Electronics Technology, or a closely related field required. A bachelor’s degree in a related field is preferred. Relevant industry certifications in manufacturing, automation, robotics, PLCs, CNC, additive manufacturing, safety, quality, or Lean/Six Sigma are preferred. Special Knowledge/Skills Knowledge of automated manufacturing systems, industrial controls, robotics, programmable logic controllers, CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and production processes. Knowledge of battery components, battery construction, battery pack assembly, manufacturing safety, quality control, and inspection practices. Ability to operate, demonstrate, maintain, and troubleshoot manufacturing and automation equipment safely. Ability to develop competency-based curriculum, laboratory activities, assessments, and instructional materials. Excellent oral and written communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts to students and incumbent workers with varied experience levels. Ability to use instructional technology, manufacturing software, and general computer applications. Strong organizational, planning, recordkeeping, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work effectively with college personnel, students, grant stakeholders, employers, and community partners. Experience Five years of directly related, current work experience in advanced manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, battery production, mechatronics, machining, industrial maintenance, or a related technical field. Previous teaching, technical training, apprenticeship, or workforce development experience is preferred. Experience in defense, aerospace, automotive, energy storage, battery manufacturing, or another advanced manufacturing environment is preferred. Major Responsibilities and Duties: Teach assigned automation and advanced manufacturing courses in accordance with approved curriculum, course competencies, College policies, and grant requirements. Develop and deliver DEAAG-supported training in battery construction, battery assembly, automated manufacturing of parts, robotics, PLC programming and troubleshooting, CNC machining, additive manufacturing, industrial controls, quality systems, and Industry 4.0 applications. Plan and organize syllabi, lesson plans, laboratory exercises, study guides, assessments, and instructional materials for classroom, laboratory, online, customized, and off-site training. Maintain accurate attendance, assessment, credentials, and student progress records and submit required reports on schedule. Evaluate student performance, provide timely feedback, and support successful completion of competencies and industry credentials. Maintain safe, organized, and effective classroom, laboratory, shop, and industrial training environments; enforce PPE and equipment safety requirements. Operate, inspect, secure, and coordinate routine care and inventory of automation, robotics, battery, machining, additive manufacturing, and related training equipment. Coordinate with Red River Army Depot, defense contractors, regional manufacturers, and other partners to align training with workforce needs. Participate in curriculum development, program review, assessment of student learning outcomes, advisory committees, recruitment, and program improvement activities. jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION:
The Opportunity
The UTMB Department of Radiology invites applications from fellowship-trained, board-certified or board-eligible cardiothoracic imaging radiologists to join our growing academic faculty. This is a rare opportunity to practice at a high-volume, technologically advanced academic medical center while contributing meaningfully to resident and fellow education, research, and the clinical mission of one of Texas's most distinguished institutions.
We welcome candidates at all career stages — from early-career radiologists seeking a strong academic foundation to experienced faculty ready to lead. UTMB is also able to assist foreign medical graduates in pursuing certification by the American Board of Radiology.
Why UTMB?
Founded in 1891, UTMB is one of Texas's oldest and most respected academic medical centers, with a tripartite mission of clinical excellence, education, and research. The Department of Radiology offers the intellectual energy and subspecialty depth of a major academic program, in a setting that balances meaningful academic contribution with a sustainable clinical practice — without the bureaucratic weight of the largest urban academic centers.
Where You'll Live
UTMB's campuses sit at the heart of one of Texas's most distinctive coastal regions. Galveston offers a historic island lifestyle with beautiful beaches, a thriving culinary and arts scene, and a storied architectural heritage. League City and Clear Lake — home of Johnson Space Center–NASA — offer outstanding suburban living with top-rated schools and easy access to Houston's world-class cultural and economic amenities. Whether you are drawn to island living, waterfront recreation, or the energy of a major metropolitan area, this region offers something genuinely exceptional.
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
The Practice
UTMB Radiology is a vibrant, collegial academic practice operating across four hospital campuses in the Houston–Galveston corridor, including our flagship John Sealy Hospital in Galveston — a Level I trauma center — and community hospitals in League City and Clear Lake. Our cardiothoracic imaging section works with state-of-the-art technology including 1.5T and 3.0T MRI, multidetector CT, and photon-counting CT.
Our department trains 8 diagnostic radiology residents per year and hosts multiple subspecialty fellowship programs, giving faculty meaningful daily opportunities for case-based teaching, mentorship, and educational engagement. Faculty benefit from close collaboration with subspecialty colleagues across a true academic medical center, with the depth of institutional infrastructure — including research support, GME infrastructure, and administrative resources — that a standalone community practice cannot offer.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
• MD or DO degree
• Board certification or eligibility by the American Board of Radiology
• Fellowship training in cardiothoracic imaging
• Certificate of Added Qualification in Cardiac CT
• Valid Texas Medical License, or ability to obtain prior to start
• Eligibility for appointment to the UTMB medical staff
• Authorization to work in the United States
SALARY:
Commensurate with experience.
COMPENSATION & BENEFTIS:
• Competitive salary, commensurate with qualifications and experience, benchmarked to Texas academic practices
• Incentive program
• Superior benefits package including health, dental, and vision coverage
• Excellent retirement program

Dr. Max Wintermark , Chair of Radiology — mawinter@utmb.edu

jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION Chair - Department of Bioinformatics and Systems Medicine, McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics (MSBMI) JOB SUMMARY: The Chair of the Department of Bioinformatics and Systems Medicine will provide visionary academic and scientific leadership for one of the nation's premier programs in AI-driven biomedical discovery. Reporting directly to the Dean, the Chair will lead approximately 15 faculty members and will be responsible for advancing the Department's research, education, faculty development, and strategic growth. The Chair will cultivate an ambitious, collaborative, and innovation-focused culture that accelerates discoveries at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computational biology, genomics, systems medicine, and precision health. Working across the McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics, UTHealth Houston, the Texas Medical Center, and national and international partners, the Chair will expand interdisciplinary research programs, develop transformative collaborations, and enhance the Department's national and global reputation. The Chair will also play a central role in shaping the future of education in bioinformatics, systems medicine, and biomedical AI by strengthening existing graduate programs and developing innovative curricula that prepare students for an AI-driven biomedical workforce. As a key member of the school’s leadership team, the Chair will work closely with the Dean to implement the school’s strategic vision of becoming a globally recognized AI-native institution for education, research, innovation, and societal impact. The successful candidate will recruit outstanding faculty, expand externally funded research, foster translational partnerships across academia, healthcare, government, and industry, and position the Department as an international leader in AI-enabled biomedical science and precision medicine. The Department of Bioinformatics and Systems Medicine is at the forefront of the AI-driven transformation of biomedical discovery and precision health. The Department develops and applies advanced artificial intelligence, computational biology, and data science to understand human biology across molecular, cellular, organ, and population scales. By integrating genomic, multi-omic, imaging, physiological, clinical, and real-world data, the Department creates next-generation computational approaches that accelerate scientific discovery, enable precision medicine, and transform healthcare. Research spans AI for genomics and precision medicine, foundation models for biology and medicine, cancer AI, computational drug discovery, single-cell and spatial omics, multimodal AI, imaging AI, biological networks and knowledge graphs, systems biology, digital biomarkers, causal and predictive modeling, and translational biomedical AI. Guided by a vision to become a global leader in AI-driven bioinformatics and systems medicine, the Department educates the next generation of scientists and innovators, develops transformative AI technologies for biomedical research and healthcare, and serves as a catalyst for interdisciplinary collaboration across basic science, translational medicine, clinical care, and industry. Located within the Texas Medical Center, the world's largest medical complex, the Department benefits from unparalleled opportunities for collaborative research, clinical translation, entrepreneurship, and innovation. The incoming Chair will have exceptional institutional support for strategic program development, faculty recruitment, interdisciplinary partnerships, and the expansion of an internationally recognized program in AI-enabled biomedical discovery. APPOINTMENTS/BENEFITS: The Chair of the Department of Bioinformatics and Systems Medicine at the McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics is a full-time faculty position. Resources for intra- and trans-departmental program development, faculty recruitment, and cross-campus collaborations are available.POSITIO

jobs.description: Are you interested in building a career that makes a difference and creates a legacy? Parker University, the fourth-fastest growing college in Texas and the fastest-growing college in Dallas, is currently searching for a Clinic Faculty Doctor to join our rapidly expanding team! We are seeking individuals who desire to use their unique skills to innovate and make an impact. The Clinic Faculty Doctor is responsible for providing quality chiropractic care to patients in a manner that educates and mentors chiropractic interns to serve as patient-centered chiropractic physicians and members of a collaborative interdisciplinary healthcare team. WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING: Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Course/Pod Management: Faculty members are responsible to design, deliver and manage their course in accordance with the guidance provided to them by their direct supervisor. This includes, but is not limited to, the following: Adhere to the syllabus. Clearly communicate course requirements, means of evaluation, deadlines, and policies to students. Hold clinic-related classes as scheduled, take attendance and submit it timely. Develop high-quality means of evaluating student learning outcomes and apply them fairly and consistently in accordance with Parker policies, as well as methods and timelines set forth in the syllabus. Submit grades and required course documentation timely. Follow Parker policies and procedures in all elements of course management. Evaluate interns individually on the basis of clinical skill, attitude, attendance, knowledge and patient management. Demonstrate quality clinical decision-making and documentation relevant to the clinic policies. Maintain adequate patient volume. Facilitate student participation in marketing activities. Student/Patient Interaction: Faculty members generally have more direct contact with students than any other institutional employee and are responsible for managing that contact consistent with the highest ethical and professional standards. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries with students and patients. Respond timely to student e-mails and voicemails. Maintain required office hours to provide additional academic and clinical support to students and go over assessments and other graded work. Fairly and consistently apply Parker clinic and student conduct policies. Clinics: Lead a team of interns in the service of patients and the community by ensuring the efficient care of patients and educating the community on health-related service and topics Develop and execute a plan for attracting new patients for the Parker University Chiropractic Clinics and the intern team Assist in programs for orienting new interns to the clinical experience Identify the need and recommend additional instructions to interns found deficient in any aspect of patient care Report severely deficient interns to the Dean of Clinics Monitor intern progress toward clinical requirements for graduation and aid the intern in fulfilling said requirements. Comply with Clinic policies and procedures. Maintain high levels of patient satisfaction. Curricular and Programmatic Quality, Integrity and Review: The faculty, within the framework provided by programmatic accreditation standards and institutional vision and mission, has responsibility for curricular maintenance and improvement. Assist in vertical and horizontal integration of curriculum. Participate in Quality Enhancement Project, OSCE exams, and other activities designed to evaluate student learning outcomes. Contribute to maintenance and/or improvement of programmatic outcomes such as National Board scores, Student Satisfaction Surveys, Graduate Exit Surveys, etc. Clinics: Have thorough knowledge of Parker quality patient care including the use of chiropractic adjusting, neuromuscular therapeutic exercise and activity, diagnostic imaging and body chemistry testing, nutrition and supplementation, and advising patients on therapeutic lifesty

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant Professor
jobs.college: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
jobs.description:
The School of Health Professions at UT Health San Antonio is recruiting for a certified physician assistant with excellent clinical skills who are interested in staffing our acute care clinic on the weekends.
This is a flexible, prn position, starting with two to three 8-hour shifts per month, depending on individual provider interest and availability.
The selected provider will be expected to staff the School of Health Professions Saturday and/or Sunday acute care clinic.
Initial employment responsibilities will include:
· Conduct patient-centric examinations and craft evidence-based workups and treatment plans within an acute care setting
· Interpret basic in-clinic laboratory tests (e.g., urinalysis/urine dipstick, quick strep, and blood glucose)
· Document patient care within standard electronic medical record application (e.g., EPIC)
· Triage and manage patient flow efficiently to minimize wait times
· Review and manage weekend tasks, including patient callbacks regarding lab results
· Consult supervising physician based on the scope of practice and patient needs
Qualified Candidates must be comfortable seeing patients aged three months and up.
The selected PA must be certified by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA), licensed by the Texas Medical Board, and must have a degree from a CAHEA, CAAHEP, or ARC-PA accredited physician assistant program.
Primary care or urgent care experience is preferred but not required.
This position offers a competitive salary and flexible schedule.
UT Health San Antonio is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer including protected veterans and persons with disabilities. All faculty appointments are designated as security sensitive positions.

jobs.description: Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor in PsychologyApply now DescriptionThe Department of Psychology at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a full-time, 9-month, non-tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Clinical Assistant Professor or Clinical Associate Professor, to begin January or August 2027. We seek a highly qualified clinician-educator with a strong commitment to evidence-based clinical practice and training. Overview The Clinical Psychology program at The University of Texas at Austin follows a clinical science model and is aligned with the principles of the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), emphasizing the integration of rigorous scientific training with high-quality, evidence-based clinical practice. This role centers on training graduate students in evidence-based clinical practice within a clinical science model and offers the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to a strong and collaborative training environment. The successful candidate will contribute to our Clinical Psychology Ph.D. program primarily through psychological assessment training, clinical supervision, undergraduate and graduate teaching, and program service. Responsibilities will include: Teaching graduate-level courses, including some combination of intellectual, ADHD, personality, neuropsychological and related assessment topics Teaching undergraduate courses aligned with departmental priorities and the candidate’s expertise. Providing clinical supervision in psychological assessment with emphasis on integrated report writing, case conceptualization, and diagnostic formulation. Contributing to graduate clinical training in evidence-based psychotherapy, consistent with program needs and the candidate’s expertise. Participating in program service, including admissions, evaluation of clinical competencies, re-accreditation procedures, and curricular development. Helping maintain a strong, collaborative training environment. The 9-month instructional load is three courses in each long semester and will include a combination of classroom instruction and clinical supervision. Initial professional-track faculty appointments are typically for one year and may be renewed based on performance for up to three years at which time the position will be reviewed. About the Department The Department of Psychology is committed to fostering a culture of excellence in teaching, training, and collegial engagement. Clinical Track faculty benefit from a clear career ladder, representation on the Executive Committee, and active participation in the intellectual and service life of the department. Faculty in these roles are evaluated primarily on teaching and clinical supervision and secondarily on contributions in areas such as research, mentorship, and service. Participation in scholarly research and service activities is expected to comply with CAPTE expectations. Duties also include demonstrating knowledge, skill, and pedagogical expertise to teaching or co-teaching didactic and immersive lab courses related to areas of expertise; having the ability to interact effectively with students, administration, faculty, and staff; ensuring the delivery of curriculum based on evidence, contemporary clinical practice, and CAPTE requirements; establishing and implementing a scholarly agenda; promoting, helping, planning, and participating in community and university service. This non-tenure track faculty position supports a hybrid Doctor of Physical Therapy program. Positions may be filled at the Clinical Assistant Professor or Clinical Associate Professor rank based on qualifications and program needs. Multiple start dates are anticipated to support phased program development, curriculum delivery, laboratory immersion experiences, accreditation activities, and student progression across the eight-semester curriculum. jobs.title: Director of the Betty and Jacob Friedman Holistic Garden and Lecturer in BioSciences
jobs.description: Rice University: Wiess School of Natural Sciences Location Houston, Texas Open Date Sep 17, 2026 Description The Opportunity Rice University invites applications and nominations for the position of Director of the Betty and Jacob Friedman Holistic Garden and Lecturer in BioSciences located in Houston, Texas, with an anticipated start date of January 1, 2027. We are seeking an entrepreneurial, operationally minded leader to direct the daily site operations, educational program, strategic vision, and community integration of this dynamic academic urban farm. This role requires a dynamic "academic entrepreneur" who possesses advanced horticultural knowledge, physical site management capabilities, charismatic teaching skills, and collaborative, start-up-style business acumen. Operating at the intersection of practical horticulture, academic instruction, and interdisciplinary outreach, the Director will manage daily urban farm activities, budget allocation, organic crop production, and site infrastructure—including a greenhouse, solar array, rainwater collection, apiary, and composting systems. They will lead and mentor a team comprising a full-time Post-Graduate Fellow/Manager and student workers. As Lecturer in BioSciences, the Director will design and deliver popular undergraduate coursework in horticulture, sustainable agriculture, and related practitioner fields each semester. Crucially, the Director will establish a strategic vision for generating revenue through produce sales, public workshops, and plant sales, while expanding volunteer initiatives, alumni and donor engagement, and community food system outreach. Beyond campus, the Director will serve as a strategic bridge builder—forging high-impact research, clinical health, and public partnerships across Rice University and the neighboring Texas Medical Center in areas such as garden therapy, public health, and patient wellness. Required Qualifications Candidates must have a master’s degree in Public Horticulture, Sustainable Agriculture, or a related practitioner field; or a Ph.D. in Horticulture or a related discipline by the start date. They must have a proven track record in site operations, budget oversight, crop management, volunteer coordination, and inspirational educational instruction. Procedure for Candidacy To apply, please submit the following materials online https://apply.interfolio.com/193817: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) experience and vision statement covering operational leadership, crop management, and staff supervision (2 pages max); (4) statement of teaching philosophy (1 page max); and (5) contact information for three references. The experience and vision statement and statement of teaching philosophy may also include plans for fostering an equitable and inclusive learning environment and a gardening team. Applications that are received by November 16, 2026 will receive full consideration, but we will continue reviewing applications until positions are filled. For additional information, please visit our website here or contact Dominique Oumar (dominique.oumar@rice.edu), Director of Administrative Operations of the Wiess School of Natural Sciences. About Rice Rice University is a private, coeducational, nonsectarian university that aspires to path-breaking research, unsurpassed teaching, and contributions to the betterment of our world. Rice fulfills this mission by cultivating a diverse community of learning and discovery that produces leaders across the spectrum of human endeavor. In our candidate pools, we seek to attract greater representation of women, scholars of color, people with disabilities, veterans, and others who have historically been underrepresented in the health sciences; accelerate progress in building a faculty and staff varied in background and thought; and maintain an environment that fosters interaction and understanding within our community. jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston is seeking applications from highly qualified candidates for the position of Chief of MRI Research and Director of the Magnetic Resonance Imaging Center. This is a senior position, Associate Professor or Professor, requiring leadership and administrative skills. The MRI Center houses UPMR790 3Tpet/mr and Bruker Biospec 7T animal scanners. Courses may be taught on a high school campus, college campus, online, or in a hybrid format. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Teach assigned dual credit courses in accordance with approved college curriculum, syllabi, learning outcomes, and academic policies. Maintain appropriate academic rigor consistent with college-level expectations. Develop and deliver engaging instruction that promotes student learning and success. Evaluate student performance through assignments, exams, projects, and participation. Submit grades, attendance, and required reports in a timely manner. Maintain regular communication with students, high school partners, department leadership, and college administration as needed. Utilize the institution’s learning management system and instructional technologies. Adhere to all institutional policies, FERPA requirements, and applicable state/federal regulations. Participate in orientation, training, and meetings as requested. Support student retention, persistence, and academic integrity. Maintain required credentials and documentation for accreditation compliance. Perform other related duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Master’s degree in the teaching discipline or a master’s degree with at least 18 graduate semester hours in the teaching discipline. Demonstrated subject matter expertise. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work effectively with high school students, parents, faculty, and school district personnel. Commitment to student success and academic excellence. Ability to use instructional technology and learning management systems. Preferred Qualifications Prior college-level teaching experience. Experience teaching dual credit or early college students. Online teaching experience. Familiarity with SACSCOC or other regional accreditation faculty credentialing standards. Secondary education teaching experience or partnership experience with school districts. Work Environment Courses may be taught at partner high schools, on campus, or online. Evening or daytime teaching assignments may be available depending on scheduling needs. Travel to partner sites may be required. Physical Requirements Ability to communicate effectively in classroom and virtual settings. Ability to sit or stand for extended periods during instruction. Ability to operate standard classroom and computer equipment. Compensation Compensation is based on course load, credentials, experience, and institutional adjunct pay schedules. Additional Information Adjunct appointments are part-time, term-based, and contingent upon enrollment, program needs, and successful completion of credentialing requirements. Equal Opportunity Statement McMurry University is committed to an educational and working environment that provides equal opportunity to all members of the university community and prohibits unlawful discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, age, genetic information, disability or veteran status, in employment or the provision of services, in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws. Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation is also prohibited pursuant to University policy.Link to This JobLocationTexas (Remote)DepartmentEnrollment Management AdministrationEmployment TypeFull-TimeMinimum ExperienceEntry-levelPrivacy Policy • Terms of Service • © BambooHR All rights reserved.

jobs.description: EDUC/PSYC 1300 Learning Frameworks Faculty Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Position Details Position Information Working Title EDUC/PSYC 1300 Learning Frameworks Faculty Position Status Full Time Department School of Liberal Arts and Education General Summary The in-person EDUC/PSYC 1300 Learning Frameworks faculty member is responsible for providing instruction in essential academic skills that support student success and college readiness, including learning strategies, critical thinking, time management, goal setting, and effective study habits. The course is designed to foster a student-centered learning environment that promotes engagement, self-awareness, motivation, and persistence. Faculty guide students in connecting with campus resources and support their transition into college-level coursework while encouraging academic achievement and long-term success. Specific Position Duties Maintains up-to-date knowledge for EDUC/PSYC 1300, with a specific specialization in the study, research, and theory of the psychology of learning, cognition, and motivation; factors that impact learning; and the application of learning strategies. Demonstrates willingness and ability to teach various courses, times, locations, and delivery methods, as needed and as reasonably requested by the college. Utilizes appropriately challenging coursework to help students realize their full potential as learners. Provides students with written expectations. Administers tests appropriate to course content, including a comprehensive final exam measuring overall grasp of course objectives. By way of instruction, affirms the worth and dignity of all persons and the right of all persons to learn. Maintains an appropriate learning and assessment climate in the classroom—whether traditional, web-based, or distance—that encourages the free exchange of ideas while upholding academic honesty and objectivity. Prepares adequately for class and arrives promptly at class meetings, labs, and other scheduled instructional activities. Delivers material in a clear and understandable manner. Addresses student concerns, questions, and input both in class and through posted office hours, timely electronic communication, and other suitable means. Teaches online and remote classes using a variety of instructional technologies. Assists with student recruitment, advising, and persistence activities, and participates in various departmental and campus-wide committees. Effectively handles routine procedures necessary for the successful day-to-day operation of the department, as delegated by the Dean. Submits required reports and schedules in a timely manner. Maintains effective relationships with professional counterparts throughout the college and the community. Works with departments and the Instructional Leadership Team to create and implement a strategic plan for continuous improvement. Ensures compliance of all courses and program offerings. Assists with the development and management of departmental grants. Performs other duties as assigned. jobs.description: Faculty Opportunities Be the catalyst for teaching and cancer research. At The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, you can join more than 1,600 distinguished clinical and research faculty members and leaders in Making Cancer History®. Our reputation, resources and renowned staff create a desirable environment for faculty across all levels of tenure. We typically recruit for faculty positions at the level of assistant professor and higher for clinical, research and physician scientists. View Clinical Faculty Positions › View Research Faculty Positions › Impressive Reach You'll work alongside some of the biggest names in cancer research, with an emphasis on cross-collaboration and teamwork. In addition, our stature provides access to a large national and international network of colleagues. Our goal is to provide you with the optimal balance of teaching, speaking and conducting research. In order to foster and protect academic freedom for activities and teaching, we offer a seven-year term tenure track that includes both Clinical Faculty Appointments and Research Faculty Appointments. Outstanding Resources We offer robust opportunities to accomplish and promote your research, and the facilities and resources you'll find at UT MD Anderson surpass those of other cancer institutes. You will have access to a wide range of cancer research resources, sophisticated tools and specialized expertise to accelerate your discoveries, right on our campus. Start-Up Funding At UT MD Anderson, we provide start-up funds from institutional resources to help initiate research programs for new faculty. Other funding opportunities are available, and we have departments and staff available to assist you with grant writing and submission and to provide training on regulations and requirements applicable to research. You will discover that the educational resources we have to advance your career are outstanding. jobs.description: Fall 2026 Co-Funded Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor in PediatricsApply now DescriptionThe College of Pharmacy at The University of Texas at Austin is dedicated to providing exemplary education, training, research, and professional development for Pharm.D. students, graduate students, and postgraduates; to advance discovery, innovation, and patient care. To help advance this mission, we are seeking a distinguished applicant to fill one professional-track (non-tenure), clinical faculty position at the rank of assistant or associate professor (depending on qualifications) for a full-time Pediatrics faculty position. This position is located in Austin, Texas, and will be co-funded (50/50) with Dell Children’s Medical Center (DCMC) and the College of Pharmacy at The University of Texas at Austin, with a practice site at DCMC. Dell Children’s in Austin, Texas is a 299-bed academic facility with a level 1 Trauma designation and national ranking in 7 specialties. The practice site provides a wide variety of pediatric acute care, including cardiology, neurology, oncology, surgical, maternal-fetal medicine, heart and kidney transplantation, and advanced critical care treatment, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The successful applicant will facilitate practice laboratories, provide classroom instruction, mentor, and supervise clinical clerkships for students in the Pharm.D. program. Clinical service that supports resident and Pharm.D. student education as well as the goals of the DCMC pharmacy department is expected. Faculty members will provide service to the college, hospital, university, and broader professional community and will contribute to the operational success of the Pharmacy Department, as appropriate. The primary practice focus of this position will be in alignment with candidate interests and departmental priorities at Dell Children’s Medical Center. Potential practice areas include, but are not limited to, inpatient internal medicine, inpatient cardiology, and/or outpatient specialty care (e.g. anticoagulation). The faculty member will be expected to supervise pharmacy students and residents to help them learn to care for hospitalized pediatric patients with acute and chronic conditions. The successful individual will have interests in developing interprofessional collaborations to advance pharmacy practice, research, and scholarship. QualificationsCandidates must: have an earned Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an ACPE-accredited school of pharmacy; be licensed or be eligible for licensure in the State of Texas; have successfully completed a Pediatric PGY-1 and PGY-2 specialty practice residency (preferred) or equivalent experience by the start date (by August 1, 2026); and be able to demonstrate effective teaching.Application InstructionsInterested persons should include a cover letter, a detailed curriculum vitae, and three (3) confidential letters of recommendation. Review of applications will continue until position is filled, with a priority application date of March 8, 2026. jobs.description:
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
The UTMB Department of Family Medicine was founded as an independent department in 1971 but existed prior to that as a division of the Department of Preventive Medicine and Population Health. Family Medicine faculty provide medical care to Galveston County residents through its three clinics, located on the UTMB Galveston campus, on the western end of Galveston Island, and in Dickinson, Texas, and through its inpatient service at the new Jennie Sealy Hospital in Galveston, Texas. Additional services are rendered at the Gulf Health Care Center nursing home and the Galveston County Health District's Coastal Health & Wellness. At present the Department includes programs in medical student education, residency, faculty development, and research.
This position will be 90% clinical and 10% education and will see patients in the clinic primarily at our Galveston Island locations. He/she will provide direct patient care and will provide teaching and supervision of Family Medicine residents. This physician may share on-call responsibilities, including evening and weekend hours, precept medical students and cover other clinical services as needed. He/she may provide comprehensive health care with enhanced access for patients within a patient-centered medical home clinical model. This faculty will have 90% clinical effort and practice primarily at the Island West Clinic (IW) but will also rotate through the Island West (IE) or Dickinson Family Medicine Clinics as departmental need arises.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
• MD or DO degree
• A strong commitment to research, patient care, medical student, and resident education.
• U.S. Citizenship or Employment Authorization to work in the U.S.

Commensurate with experience

jobs.title: Health Policy (Assistant Professor)
jobs.description: Health Policy (Assistant Professor)Apply now DescriptionThe Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs at the University of Texas at Austin (“LBJ School”) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Health Policy to begin in Fall of academic year 2027-28 (with an August 2027 start date). One of the nation’s top programs in public affairs, the LBJ School is seeking to strengthen its faculty in health policy design, implementation, and evaluation. The LBJ School comprises more than 50 faculty members and approximately 350 graduate students, and a new undergraduate degree that will eventually serve another 500 students. It offers multi-disciplinary curricula leading to the degrees of Bachelor of Arts of Public Affairs, Master of Public Affairs, Master of Global Policy Studies, Master of National Security, and Ph.D. in Public Policy. The ideal candidate will possess proven experience and expertise in one or more of the following areas: healthcare systems, healthcare policy reforms, health services research, and the effects of policy on health (e.g. policies affecting the socioeconomic or environmental determinants of health). The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Video Game Art and Animation is a new degree within the Department of Visual and Performing Arts. The ideal candidate will be able to help shape this degree for the next generation of video game artists. Applications will be accepted continuously and reviewed as instructional needs develop.Ideal candidates will demonstrate strong abilities in art, creativity, design, and technology, supported by professional or academic experience in game design, technical art, real-time production, and game development processes. They should be capable of integrating visual arts with technology and teaching students how visual design, 3D modeling and asset creation, animation, lighting, materials, shaders, optimization, and interactive features function together in professional game-production settings.They will also mentor students with backgrounds in graphic design, digital art, and traditional fine arts. Create curriculum for new courses within theVGAAcurriculum to include both online and face-to-face modalities. Other art courses as assigned. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Proficiency in 2D and 3D digital art tools used in contemporary game and animation production. Proficiency in 3D asset creation and integration, procedural production techniques, lighting, materials, shaders, rigging, animation systems, artist-oriented scripting, AI-supported creative workflows, XR optimization, and other commonly used tools and processes associated with game development and real-time production. Ability to recruit, retain students in the Video Game Art and Animation concentration. Participate in departmental/Art Area meetings and events. Maintain regular office hours. Work collaboratively and productively with faculty colleagues to meet the needs of students and the Art Program. Strong technical proficiency with Unreal Engine, Microsoft Visual Studio, C++, C#, Python, JavaScript, HLSL/GLSL, Verse, Advanced Blueprint Visual Scripting, computer graphics math, performance profiling, and specialized pipelines like Niagara VFX, animation and rendering. Familiarity with industry-standard software, tools, and production workflows, including Autodesk Maya, Mudbox, Adobe Substance 3D, Adobe Creative Cloud, Blender, and ZBrush. Physical Requirements Standing/sitting, bending, lifting, carrying as necessary per the job duties. jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston, a leading academic health center, invites applications for a full-time Genetic Counselor, non-tenure clinical track Instructor, or Assistant Professor position in the Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Reproductive Sciences. The selected faculty member will provide genetic counseling to individuals whose genetic background may pose hereditary risks to their children and coordinate communication between the patient and the multidisciplinary team during diagnosis and evaluation of these conditions. Position Key Accountabilities: Obtains patient and family historical medical data and interprets data obtained to determine possible problem areas.Assists patients in understanding genetic diseases or birth defects to provide professional counseling services.Assesses patient needs related to emotional stress, fear of test results, financial or transportation issues, marital conflicts, or patient-physician conflicts to make proper referral recommendations.Updates the medical records and keeps team members apprised of patient problems.Refers patients for tests or to other assistance, such as a social worker.Monitors information resulting from test results and agency referrals and reviews cases for further evaluation to assure continuity of patient care and education of the patient's family about the disease/problem.Performs other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Current board certification or board eligibility by the American Board of Medical Genetics or American Board of Genetic Counselors. Master's degree in human genetics and counseling or a related field.No experience required.

jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION The Department of Anesthesiology and Center for Perioperative Medicine (CPM) at McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston would like to invite applications for non-tenure instructor and assistant professor faculty positions. Further information on our multidisciplinary research environment, department resources, and research programs is available on our website: https://med.uth.edu/anesthesiology/research/center-for-perioperative-medicine/. An attractive start-up package, competitive salary, and generous benefits will be provided. Position Key Accountabilities: Responsibilities include developing extramural funding and actively participating in research activities of the IPM. We are particularly interested in applicants with independent funding who are passionate about pursuing translational research in endogenous adaptive responses related to the field of perioperative medicine and critical care including acute lung injury, myocardial or hepatic ischemia, acute kidney injury, and intestinal inflammation. Qualifications: MD or Ph.D. degree4 years of additional research experience. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to excellence, discovery, and service, have the potential to be outstanding in their field of expertise, and share an interest in fulfilling the common goals of McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston.Please submit a cover letter, full curriculum vitae, description of future research plans, and at least three reference letters. For additional information, please contact Yanyu Wang, Director of Management Operations, Research. E-mail: Yanyu.Wang@uth.tmc.edu.
